sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 is the south-western corner of the Montclair volume, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. A diagonal dash-dot line labelled Town of West Orange crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right and marks the municipal boundary; ground west of it lies outside the volume and is left blank. Most of the sheet is open or sparsely built estate land on the slope of the mountain, divided into large plots. Undercliff Road enters from the right, curves south-west and joins Eagle Rock Way, which loops around a block of narrow lots before running down the sheet towards Way Side Place at the bottom. Valley crosses from the left edge to meet Eagle Rock Way, Murray is a narrow street parallel to the boundary running north from Valley, and South Mountain Av. runs east from the Eagle Rock Way junction to Llewellyn Road on the right margin. Buildings are few: a handful of detached frame dwellings with outbuildings, a hotel with a pavilion lettered City View Hotel near the top, and a stable or barn at upper right. A street at the top is lettered No Name. Wayside Place lies along the bottom edge, with block numbers 2, 3 and 4 marking the neighbouring sheets. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: A street at the top of the sheet is lettered No Name.
Valley is today's Valley Way; Undercliff Road, Eagle Rock Way, South Mountain Avenue, Llewellyn Road and Murray (Murray Street) keep their names.
Way Side Pl. is today's Wayside Place.
Georeferenced from five points only; two of them are hand-picked at curved junctions, so the placement is medium confidence.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 lies directly north of sheet 3 in the south-west of the Montclair volume, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The upper part of the sheet is open ground cut into long narrow lots, bounded above by the dash-dot Town of West Orange line. Undercliff Road runs across the upper third from the left margin to a bend near the right, where it turns south-east. South Mountain Av. crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right, with Llewellyn Road meeting it on the left and Gates Av. on the right. Below it Clinton Av. runs parallel, and Warren Pl. and Wayside Pl. lead off to the bottom edge. The built-up part is the block between South Mountain Av. and Clinton Av., where a row of detached dwellings of two and a half storeys front South Mountain Av., with a few brick-fronted and plastered houses; north of South Mountain Av. there are scattered large houses on big lots and a private stable. A street at the upper left is lettered No Name. Neighbouring sheets are named by number in the margins: 1, 3, 9 and 17. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: A street at the upper left is lettered No Name.

Gates Av. and Clinton Av. here are today's Gates Avenue and Clinton Avenue; the modern Clinton Avenue runs differently from the street drawn as Clinton Av. here, which matches it only at the junctions used.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the residential blocks between Gates Av. along the top and Eagle Rock Way and Llewellyn Road in the lower half, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Clinton Av. bounds the sheet on the left and Harrison Av. on the right. Melrose Pl. and Warren Pl. cut across the sheet from Clinton Av. to Harrison Av., and Eagle Rock Way runs down the middle, then curves round the bottom of the sheet to meet Way Side Pl. Llewellyn Road crosses from the left, bends beside Eagle Rock Way and runs south-east to Harrison Av. The blocks on the left of Eagle Rock Way are mostly large lots with a few houses and greenhouses (Hot Ho., Hot Hos. are lettered); those on the right between Gates Av. and Warren Pl. are built up with detached dwellings of two and a half storeys, and a fire alarm box is marked on Harrison Av. at both ends. Oak Pl. appears at the lower right edge. Printed block numbers 17, 2, 12, 1, 4 and 11 point to adjoining sheets. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: Way Side Pl. is today's Wayside Place; the other streets keep their names.
Eagle Rock Way's drawn course at the bottom of the sheet differs from the modern road, so the junctions there were not used.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the thinly built south-west corner of the volume beside the West Orange line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Harrison Av. runs down the right side of the sheet, curving towards the lower right edge. The left two thirds are large undivided plots, including a long block marked 5 containing the compass, and the dash-dot Town of West Orange boundary crosses the lower left diagonally. At the top, Eagle Rock Way curves across the sheet with Way Side Pl. running off the top edge. The only built ground is along Harrison Av.: a florist's establishment lettered J. C. Williams, Florist with hot water boilers and long greenhouses, a few dwellings and barns, and a small group of houses on Howe Av. Further down, Howe Av., Warman and Wilfred leave Harrison Av. to the west, joined by a street lettered No Name that runs north-south. Cedar Av., Tichenor, Charles St., Finan St. and Oak Pl. are stubs lettered at the right edge where they leave towards sheet 5 and sheet 11. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: A north-south street between Howe Av. and Wilfred is lettered No Name; it is now Winfield Street.
Finan St. is today's Southern Terrace; Way Side Pl. is today's Wayside Place.
Control rests on two detected and three hand-picked points, mostly along Harrison Av.: low to medium confidence.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 continues south from sheet 11 along Harrison Av. and High, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Cedar Av. runs across the top between Harrison Av. on the left and High on the right. The only closely built area is the block between Cedar Av. and Finan, where Tichenor Pl. and Charles run in from Harrison Av. and are lined with small detached dwellings, frame outbuildings and stables, with a fire alarm box at the corner of Tichenor Pl. Further right a row of larger houses faces High. South of Finan the sheet is open farm land cut into big plots, with a street lettered No Name running across from High, and the Town of West Orange boundary crossing the lower left. Near the bottom, Virginia Av. runs from Harrison Av. across to High, Amelia and Samuel cross the lower part, and Watchung Av. runs down the right edge. The Essex Fells Dairy, with a bottling works and steam plant, stands at the bottom right, together with a group of small dwellings on Watchung Av. Howe Av., Warman St. and Wilfred St. appear as stubs leaving Harrison Av. to the west. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: A street running east from High is lettered No Name.
Finan is today's Southern Terrace; Charles is Charles Street, Amelia is Amelia Street and High is High Street.
Samuel east of High is now Hilltop Place; Watchung Av. here is today's Enfield Avenue.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the narrow wedge of mostly open land between High on the left and Orange Road on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Cedar Av. runs across the top from High to Orange Road, and Pleasant Av. runs down the middle of the sheet from Cedar Av. to Walnut Pl. at the bottom. Watchung Av. and Virginia Av. leave High at the lower left, and Samuel runs from High to Pleasant Av. Washington Av., Grenada Pl. and Linden Av. enter Orange Road from the right. The land is divided into big lots with long narrow plots on either side of Pleasant Av. in the lower half. Buildings are sparse: a group of dwellings and outbuildings in the top left near Cedar Av. with servants' quarters and coops, a larger house marked Admittance Refused, a conservatory and greenhouse on Orange Road at the bottom, and a fire alarm box on Cedar Av. A street running east from High is lettered No Name. The dash-dot boundary of the Town of West Orange cuts the lower left corner. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: A street running east from High is lettered No Name.
Walnut Pl. is today's Ward Place; Samuel here is now Hilltop Place; Watchung Av. is today's Enfield Avenue; Finan Street is Southern Terrace.
The east end of Samuel was not used as control: the modern Hilltop Place continues beyond Pleasant Av. where the sheet draws none.

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 is the lower left of the sheet, set off from the upper right part by a heavy double line, and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It lies on the Town of West Orange side, along the boundary line shown dash-dot near the left edge, with the City of Orange beyond it. Orange Road runs from the lower left corner north-east across the sheet to the junction with Walnut Pl. and Pleasant Way, where a fire alarm box is marked. Pleasant Av. and Samuel run diagonally in the upper left from the heavy line, with Watchung Av. and High St. at the top left corner where a few small dwellings stand on narrow lots. Between them a wedge of lots is laid out along Pleasant Way and Walnut Pl. with a scatter of detached dwellings. The large block marked 2 in the middle is Rosedale Cemetery, left blank. In the lower left a group of houses stands along Orange Road beside the boundary, and at the foot of the sheet Coogan St., Willow and Cross St. appear beyond a brook drawn in blue, which crosses the lower half from the left. The dash-dot boundary lettered Glen Ridge Borough Essex Co. Vol. Two crosses the bottom right, beyond which the map continues in another volume. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; water pipes, hydrants and street widths are lettered in the streets.
notes: Walnut Pl. is today's Ward Place; Samuel is now Hilltop Place. Detail drawn about 10 percent shorter east-west than modern streets, so only three control points were detected (see the sheet note).
A lettered Printing building stands at the lower left.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (lower left: Pleasant Av, Pleasant Way, Walnut Pl = Ward Place, Orange Road, Rosedale Cemetery, to the Glen Ridge and West Orange lines; north to upper right) and part 2 (upper right: Orange Road, Linden Av, Grenada Pl, Willowdale Av, Washington Av; north to the right). Part 1 drawn geometry disagrees with modern by about 10 percent; 3 points only.

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 7 is the upper right of the sheet, divided from part 1 by a heavy double line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the right as the compass arrow in the upper middle shows. Orange Road enters from the upper right and sweeps across the top of the part to the left, where it runs beside the heavy line. Linden Av. runs south from Orange Road across the part and meets Willowdale Av. near a brook drawn in blue, crossed by a footbridge lettered Frame Bridge; the brook then runs eastwards along the foot of the part to Washington Av. on the right edge. Grenada Pl. lies between Linden Av. and Washington Av., and Willowdale Av. crosses from left to right. The ground north of Willowdale Av. is divided into regular narrow lots, many of them empty; there is a short row of attached or closely set dwellings on the east side of Linden Av. and a few scattered houses and a large dwelling and outbuildings on Orange Road. South of the brook the plots are larger and mostly empty. Franklin Pl. and Douglas Road appear at the right edge, and the dash-dot Glen Ridge Borough line runs along the bottom. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; water pipes, hydrants and street widths are lettered in the streets.
notes: Printed Willowdale Av. and Linden Av. keep their names today.
Drawn east-west distances are shorter than modern ones, as on part 1.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (lower left: Pleasant Av, Pleasant Way, Walnut Pl = Ward Place, Orange Road, Rosedale Cemetery, to the Glen Ridge and West Orange lines; north to upper right) and part 2 (upper right: Orange Road, Linden Av, Grenada Pl, Willowdale Av, Washington Av; north to the right). Part 1 drawn geometry disagrees with modern by about 10 percent; 3 points only.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the district between Orange Road along the top and the Glen Ridge borough line near the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Washington Av. bounds the sheet on the left and Lincoln on the right. Madison Av. and Willowdale Av. cross the sheet from left to right, and Draper Terrace, Gardiner Pl., Jefferson Pl. and Sears Pl. run between them. A brook, drawn in blue, enters near the top, loops round the left side of the sheet and joins Washington Av. at the bottom left of Willowdale Av. The streets are lined with detached frame dwellings of two and a half storeys on regular lots, thickest along Madison Av., Orange Road and Irving, with larger plots and more open ground south of Willowdale Av. Franklin Pl. and Douglas Road run in the lower part and the dash-dot line lettered Glen Ridge Borough Essex Co. Vol. Two crosses the sheet, beyond which the map continues in another volume. Cedar Av. and Maple Av. are stubs lettered at the edges, and a fire alarm box stands at the lower right. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, so only a few blocks of ground fit on the sheet; water pipes and their sizes, hydrants (D.H.) and street widths are lettered in the streets, and lot numbers and block numbers are marked on the plots.
notes: Irving is today's Irving Street and Lincoln is Lincoln Street.
Drawn about 3.5 percent smaller than modern streets under parcel-based control: parcel centres are displaced here, so the part is fitted with use_parcels false.
The map continues south of the borough line in Essex Co. Vol. Two.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 lies in the south-west corner of Montclair on the slope of Orange Mountain, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Most of the sheet is open, unbuilt ground divided into large tracts by dotted and solid property lines. The boundary between Montclair, the Town of West Orange and Verona Township crosses the upper half as a dash-dot line, and Afterglow Avenue is drawn across the top with dashed edges, a laid-out road with no houses on it. Close to the boundary a small group of lots is numbered as blocks 1 to 3. The built part is confined to the lower third. Gates Avenue runs down the left margin to South Mountain Avenue along the bottom edge, with Undercliff Road leaving it near the top of the built area and running east, where the sheet prints (Lloyd Road) beside the name. Union leaves the bend of Undercliff Road and runs south to South Mountain Avenue. The lots along these roads carry a handful of large detached dwellings with their stables, coach houses and outbuildings, a few in pink, and a larger house with a cluster of outbuildings on the Gates Avenue frontage, with a water pipe laid in each road and hydrants marked. Street widths of 50 to 60 feet are lettered at corners. The numbers of the adjoining sheets are given in the margins: 2 to the west, 10 to the east and 17 beyond South Mountain Avenue. A compass rose with a north arrow sits in the open upper left.
notes: The sheet prints (Lloyd Road) as a second name on the eastern stretch of Undercliff Road; modern Lloyd Road continues that road.
Only two junctions were detected (Gates Avenue and Union at South Mountain Avenue); the Undercliff Road junction with Gates Avenue was hand-picked, so the placement is low confidence.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 continues the south-western edge of Montclair east of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It is a narrow band of mostly undeveloped hillside between Afterglow Avenue, which curves across the top of the sheet, and South Mountain Avenue along the bottom. The boundary of Verona Township and the Town of West Orange runs down the left side and across the middle as a dash-dot line, and the upper two thirds of the sheet is blank ground cut by dotted property lines and the lines of large tracts numbered 0, 1 and 2. Below the boundary Undercliff Road, with Lloyd Road lettered in brackets beside it, crosses the full width of the sheet from left to right, with a row of lots on both sides. These are large frontages, each holding one detached frame dwelling, some with stables and outbuildings; two buildings are shown in pink. Hoburg Place, a 50 foot street, leaves Undercliff Road at the right and runs south to South Mountain Avenue, with a few vacant lots beside it. A water pipe is laid in the road and hydrants are marked. The scale bar is at the lower right and a compass rose with a north arrow near the top left. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 9, 17, 19 and 21.
notes: A street lettered ...YRTLE AVE. at the lower margin, beside sheet 17, is cut by the sheet edge and is not listed.

Placed from a single junction (Hoburg Place and Lloyd Road) with the scale taken from neighbouring sheets and the rotation from the measured street lines; low confidence. The modern Hoburg Place and South Mountain Avenue junction lies about 5 percent nearer than the drawn street end, so it was left out.
The sheet prints Lloyd Road in brackets as a second name for Undercliff Road.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers a block of large residential and estate land at the western edge of Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Harrison Avenue runs across the top of the sheet and Llewellyn Road down the right side, meeting Orange Road and Elm Street at a fire alarm box at the right edge. Cedar Avenue forms the left side of the sheet, High crosses it east to west and curves round to join Orange Road, and Orange Road runs diagonally along the bottom. Oak Place, a 50 foot street, divides two large parcels numbered 1 and 2 between Harrison Avenue and High, most of which is unbuilt. Houses cluster along Harrison Avenue at the upper right, along Cedar Avenue and in the lower left block between High and Orange Road, where the lots are narrow. The institutions are the Excelsior Hose Company No. 2, a volunteer fire company with a hose house on Cedar Avenue at Harrison Avenue, the Cedar Avenue Presbyterian Church and the Cedar Avenue School. A stone building, tinted blue, stands in the right-hand parcel near the curve of High. Pleasant Avenue is lettered at the lower left, Draper Terrace at the bottom and Irving Street at the lower right where it leaves Orange Road. Street widths of 50 to 66 feet are lettered, water pipes are shown in every street, and the adjoining sheets named are 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12 and 13.
notes: The modern nodes Llewellyn Road with Orange Road and Elm Street with Orange Road lie 5 m apart, but the sheet draws one four-way junction; the Llewellyn Road and Orange Road node was excluded.
Fit residuals of about 2 to 3 m at most junctions and leave-one-out near 5 m: medium confidence.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the area around the Orange Road and Gates Avenue crossing on the western side of Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned: the compass rose near the top shows north towards the upper left. Orange Road runs in a straight diagonal from the Hawthorne Place and Porter Place corner at the top to the Llewellyn Road corner at the lower right. Gates Avenue crosses it from the left edge and bends to the north-east along the right side of the sheet, where it is lined with a dense row of detached frame houses on narrow lots. South Fullerton Avenue runs from Hawthorne Place at the top down to Gates Avenue, and Harrison Avenue forms the left margin. Elm runs along the right edge. Cross is a short street of small houses at the upper left, and the Childrens Home, a large institution with its own grounds, stands between Cross and Gates Avenue. A florist, Wallace, with a long range of greenhouses, occupies a lot on Orange Road, and a pink building marked as a cellar being built stands near Llewellyn Road at the bottom. Large lots with few buildings fill the lower left. Prospect Terrace is lettered at the top right. Block numbers 1 to 3 appear, and the adjoining sheets named in the margins are 3, 7, 11, 13 and 18.
notes: Two short streets at the left edge, lettered ...ARREN PL. and ...ROSE PL., are cut by the sheet edge and are not listed; they correspond to modern Warren Place and Melrose Place.
The compass rose shows north to the upper left; the fit rotation is about -21 degrees.
The modern nodes Llewellyn Road with Orange Road and Elm Street with Orange Road were not detected; the sheet draws one junction there.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the blocks between Elm and Maple Avenue on the western side of Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Elm runs along the top of the sheet and Orange Road enters at the upper left, curving round to the fire alarm box at the corner of Lincoln and Elm. Lincoln runs down the left side of the sheet and Elmwood Avenue and Lexington Avenue run down the right side, crossing Irving and Maple Avenue. Woodland Avenue forms the lower right edge and Willowdale Avenue crosses near the bottom. The district is residential: a regular grid of 60 to 66 foot streets with frame dwellings on lots of 50 feet and more, strongest along Lexington Avenue and in the block between Elm and Irving, while the block between Irving and Maple Avenue and the blocks to the south are thinly built. Wm. Alworth and Son, general trucking, with a wagon house, stands on Maple Avenue at Elmwood Avenue. Monroe Place and Marston Place run south from Maple Avenue, Wheeler crosses the block between Monroe Place and Woodland Avenue, and Sears Place, a 40 foot street, branches off Orange Road at the left. Madison Avenue and Franklin Place appear at the left edge. A dash-dot line across the foot of the sheet marks the Borough of Glen Ridge boundary, with Toney's Brook beyond it at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets named are 8, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16.
notes: Lincoln and Irving are modern Lincoln Street and Irving Street; Wheeler is modern Wheeler Street.
Monroe Place and Marston Place are the same street, jogged at Willowdale Avenue on the sheet; the modern line jogs by a different amount, so they were not used.
The map shows Toney's Brook at the lower right edge; the brook is not used for control.

sheet-14-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 14 is the lower, 100 foot to an inch portion of the sheet, below the heavy line that crosses the sheet with the railroad. It covers the area between Maple Avenue at the top and the boundary of the Borough of Glen Ridge at the bottom, with north towards the upper right. Maple Avenue runs diagonally across the top from Woodland Avenue at the left to Bloomfield Avenue at the right, and Bay Street leaves it at the right. Woodland Avenue runs down the left side, with Wheeler and Willowdale Avenue crossing it, and Bloomfield Avenue runs down the right side to a crossing of the Montclair Branch of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and Toney's Brook at the foot of the sheet. The main feature is the Maple Avenue Public School, a pink brick building, in the block numbered 2. South of it lies a plot of narrow lots laid out between Center and Glen Street, with Grove Place along its east side, almost wholly vacant, and below it the Montclair Poor Farm, an almshouse with farm buildings. Few other buildings appear: a dwelling and a coal office on Bloomfield Avenue. Street widths are lettered 50 to 80 feet, and water pipes are drawn in the streets. Elmwood Avenue enters from the north at the top left, and the scale bar of 100 feet to an inch is at the lower right.
notes: Sheet 14 has two parts at different scales separated by a heavy line: this part (100 feet to an inch) and part 2 above it (50 feet to an inch), which shows a place about 1.2 km further north.
The Montclair Branch of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the lower right corner.
Center and Glen Street are the streets of a drawn subdivision that does not appear in the modern street network.

sheet-14-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 14 is the upper strip of the sheet, above the heavy line that crosses it, drawn at 50 feet to an inch (a separate scale bar reading Scale of Feet is printed below it) with north towards the upper right. It shows a different part of Montclair from the lower part, about 1.2 km further north near the Erie Railroad. Erie runs diagonally across the top of the strip from lower left to upper right, with Oak Place entering it from the north at the left and Sylvan Place at the middle. South of Erie the double and quadruple track of the Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, runs parallel to it from the left edge to the upper right corner. Below the tracks, Montclair Avenue runs across the lower half of the strip with a single row of about twelve frame dwellings on its north side, set on lots of about 50 feet, and a pink storage building belonging to the Montclair Van Company near the left. Chestnut runs down the right side of the strip and ends at Montclair Avenue. The land between the tracks and Montclair Avenue is block 1. The adjoining sheets are named in the margins: 43, 44, 48 and 29. A compass rose with a north arrow sits on the heavy line at the lower left, and the scale bar is at the right end of the line.
notes: Sheet 14 has two parts at different scales separated by a heavy line: this part (50 feet to an inch) and part 1 below it (100 feet to an inch).
Placed from two junctions only (Erie and Oak Place, and Chestnut and Montclair Avenue); scale and rotation agree with the printed scale, low to medium confidence.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows the blocks between Bloomfield Avenue and Fulton in central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned: the compass rose shows north towards the upper left. Bloomfield Avenue, the main street of the town, runs across the top of the sheet, and the numbers of the buildings on it run up to 244. Hartley Street and New run south from it on the right, crossing Washington Street and Fulton, while Elm and Union Street form the diagonal left edge. The blocks along Bloomfield Avenue hold a dense row of frame and brick stores and dwellings, including the Washington Hose Company No. 3 volunteer fire house, a town storage building, a laundry, a boarding house, and St. Marks M.E. Church. The block between Washington Street and Fulton holds St. Vincents Foundling Asylum, a large frame building with a Convent in pink, a Nurses Home and a row of dwellings on New. The block south of Fulton is thinly built with dwellings along Elm and a central strip of open lots, with Miller running down the middle. A water pipe is shown in each street, and the street widths are lettered. The foot of the sheet reaches Hawthorne Place and Elmwood Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are 13, 16, 18, 26 and 27. A scale of feet is printed at the lower left.
notes: Hartley, New, Fulton, Miller and Elm are modern Hartley Street, New Street, Fulton Street, Miller Street and Elm Street.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the compass showing north towards the upper left. It lies along the south-east side of central Montclair, between Bloomfield Avenue at the top and Elmwood Avenue at the foot. The upper left block, bounded by Bloomfield Avenue, Hartley, Washington and New Streets, carries the only commercial frontage: a grocery, a meat market, a pool room and barber, tenements and a manual training school face Bloomfield Avenue, with dwellings, sheds and the dashed outline of a foundation behind them. The strip between New Street and Mission Place is lined with small detached dwellings and tenements on narrow lots, and a short row of dwellings faces Fulton Street and Miller at lower left. East of Mission Place the sheet is taken up by block 4, a very long run of narrow, deep lots on Mission Place and Maple Avenue, each with a house or a three-storey flat building at the front and an empty rear; Pilgrim Church stands at the Bloomfield Avenue end. Grove Place is lettered as a short stub off Maple Avenue. The large blank areas at left, lower left and right are blocks that belong to the adjoining sheets (15, 14 and 13), and block 5 at the foot is open ground divided into lots. Street widths are lettered along the kerb lines (40 to 66 feet), and water pipes and hydrants are marked in every street. The scale bar is lettered "Scale of Feet".
notes: Mission Place is today's Mission Street; Hartley, Washington, Fulton, Miller and New are today's Hartley Street, Washington Street, Fulton Street, Miller Street and New Street.
Grove Place has no street of that name in the current OpenStreetMap data and was not used for control.
Scale bar reads 50 feet to an inch; the fit gives about 7.9 pixels per foot.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. It covers a residential district west of the town centre, bounded by Myrtle Avenue along the top, South Mountain Avenue on the left, Harrison Avenue and Orange Road on the right and Gates Avenue at the foot. Clinton Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, and two diagonal streets, Plymouth and Union, cross it from lower left to upper right, with Porter Place below them; Cross Street enters from the right edge near Harrison Avenue. The blocks are numbered 1 to 6. Almost every lot holds a detached frame dwelling of two or two and a half storeys, many with stables or outbuildings behind, set well back on large lots, and a long unnamed lane is lettered across block 1 on the left. The one non-residential property is a florist's range of greenhouses on Orange Road in block 3, and a single pink (brick) building stands near Harrison Avenue. A narrow wedge of land at the bottom of block 4 follows the line of Union and Porter Place. Street widths of 60 feet are lettered at the corners, and water pipes (6 inch in most streets, 12 inch in Clinton Avenue and Orange Road) and hydrants are shown throughout. Neighbouring sheets are cited in the margins as 21 above, 10 and 9 at left, 23 and 18 at right, and 2, 3 and 12 below.
notes: Plymouth, Union, Porter Place and Gates Avenue correspond to today's Plymouth Street, Union Street, Porter Place and Gates Avenue.
Dikes Lane (lettering partly cut by a building outline; read as Dikes) is a narrow lane; it was not used for control.
The scale bar reads 100 feet to an inch; fitted scale about 4.0 pixels per foot.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. It covers the junction area where Orange Road, Harrison Avenue and Porter Place meet, in the district east of Gates Avenue. A small triangular park, lettered "Park", lies between Harrison Avenue, Porter Place and Orange Road at the top. Orange Road runs diagonally up the left side of the sheet, with a narrow block of small dwellings between it and Cross, and Hawthorne Place runs down the middle past a fire alarm box. To the right are blocks 3 and 4, laid out in deep lots between Russell Terrace and South Fullerton Avenue, and St. Lukes Episcopal Church with its parish house, drawn in blue (stone or concrete) and standing at the corner of South Fullerton Avenue and Union. South of the church, Prospect Terrace and Gates Avenue cross the sheet from left to right and the lower blocks (6 and 8) are filled with rows of small dwellings, the lower ones facing Elm. Block 7, in a loop of Gates, is a large property with a stone building and several outbuildings. The large blanks at left and bottom belong to blocks 12 and 15 on other sheets. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered. Neighbouring sheets are cited as 17 above, 23 and 25 to the right, 26 at lower right and 15 and 12 below and left.
notes: Cross, Union and Elm are today's Cross Street, Union Street and Elm Street; Orange (Orange Road) and Hawthorne Place keep their names.
Lexington Avenue and Elmwood Avenue are lettered at the bottom edge and were not used for control; Elm Street was.
South Willow Street is printed "So. Willow St.".
Scale bar reads 100 feet to an inch.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. It covers the hillside at the northwest edge of Montclair, where Bloomfield Avenue climbs diagonally from the lower centre to the upper right. The township boundary with Verona is a dash-dot line that crosses the upper part of the sheet twice; the ground above it, including Afterglow Avenue and Sunset Avenue along the top, is outside Montclair and is lettered 74 or left blank. The sheet is mostly large estate lots with a scattering of detached dwellings and a few outbuildings. The principal property is the Montclair Military Academy, between Undercliff (Lloyd Road) and Walden Place, with its dormitories, gymnasium, swimming pool and school building, drawn in yellow frame and with notes on heating, lighting and fire extinguishers. Smaller dwellings line Rockledge Road, Parkhurst Place and the Upper Mountain Avenue and North Mountain Avenue frontages at right, and South Mountain Avenue, Hoburg Place and Undercliff run through the lower left. Claremont Avenue is cut by the right edge of the sheet, which continues on sheet 20. Street widths of 40 to 66 feet are lettered and water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches and hydrants are marked. Blocks 1 to 5 are numbered. Neighbouring sheets are cited as 74 above, 10 at left, 21 below, 39 at lower right and 20 at right.
notes: Clairmont Avenue is today's Claremont Avenue (the sheet prints Clairmont here; sheet 20 prints both spellings).
Undercliff is lettered with Lloyd Road in brackets and is today's Lloyd Road.

Only six control points were found on this sheet; the Bloomfield Avenue junctions at Upper Mountain Avenue and Parkhurst Place did not agree with the modern road lines (about 15 to 25 m) and were left out.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right, and continues sheet 19 to the east. It covers the high ground between Claremont Avenue on the left and the Alpine Street side on the right, across to the township line at the top. Four east-west streets cross the sheet: Crestmont Road along the top, Highland Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Upper Mountain Avenue, with North Mountain Avenue near the foot, and Van Vleck Street and Alpine Street run down from Upper Mountain Avenue. At the upper left the Montclair Hotel Company's large hotel, lettered as being built, stands on the Verona Township line beside Mountain House, a covered reservoir and a few outbuildings. Elsewhere the sheet is large private estates and a few detached dwellings on deep lots, with a railroad right of way crossing the lower left corner from Upper Mountain Avenue towards North Mountain Avenue. A building coloured blue at the top right lies on the township line. Bloomfield Avenue and Sunset Avenue are cut by the left edge. Blocks 1 to 5 are numbered, and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are given. Neighbouring sheets are cited as 74 above, 19 at left, 40 below and 51 at right.
notes: The sheet prints both Claremont (top) and Clairmont (lower) for the same avenue, today's Claremont Avenue.
Van Vleck and Alpine are today's Van Vleck Street and Alpine Street.
The lettered Railroad Right of Way is not a street and is not in the street list.

sheet-21-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 21 is the lower part of the sheet, below the heavy railroad line that crosses it from lower left to upper right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. It enlarges the stretch of Orange Road alongside the railroad, in the district around Church and Trinity south-east of the town centre. Orange Road runs along the railroad with a row of dwellings on its southern side; Myrtle Avenue runs down the middle of the part past a livery stable and flats, and Plymouth runs along the left side. Trinity crosses the foot, with The Crescent entering from below. At the right, Church runs down the side of block 4 and Valley Road is lettered at the right edge. Block 4 has dwellings along Orange Road and a mix of shops, a tailor, storage buildings and a vault along Church, while the Swedish Baptist Church stands on the corner near Trinity. Block 3 at lower left holds a large frame dwelling, flats and a livery. Orange Avenue and Hillside Avenue appear at the upper right across the railroad. Fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked, along with water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and street widths of 60 and 66 feet. The same ground is also drawn at 100 feet to an inch in part 2 above the railroad. Neighbouring sheets are cited as 17 at left, 22 at right, 23 below and 24 at lower right.
notes: The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch while part 2 of the same sheet is at 100 feet; both show the Myrtle Avenue and Orange Road junctions.
Plymouth is today's Plymouth Street (East Plymouth Street beyond Orange Road) and Trinity is today's Trinity Place; Church Street near the right edge has been rebuilt as Church Plaza.

Two of the four control points (Myrtle Avenue / Orange Road, Church / Hillside / Orange Road) were hand picked from the crossings of the water pipes lettered in the streets, since the detector found no street lines there.

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 21 is the upper part, above the heavy railroad line that crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It covers the blocks between South Mountain Avenue along the top and Orange Road and the railroad at the foot, in the west part of the town. Myrtle Avenue runs down the left side, with Hillside running down the middle from South Mountain Avenue to Orange Road and Church Street, and Saint Lukes Place crossing to Bloomfield Avenue at the upper right. The left blocks (1) are lined with detached frame dwellings on deep lots, among them Hillside House, a boarding house with its stable. Block 2 between Hillside and Bloomfield Avenue holds dwellings and outbuildings, and the Cloverside School, a private school with a school house, stands beside Bloomfield Avenue. The large block 22 in the middle is blank because it is drawn on sheet 22, and the scale bar and compass are placed in it. Orange Avenue and Orange Road run along the railroad at the foot. Street widths of 40 to 66 feet are lettered and water pipes and hydrants are marked. The same ground is also drawn at 50 feet to an inch in part 1 below the railroad. Neighbouring sheets are cited as 10 above, 19 at upper right, 39 beyond Bloomfield Avenue, 17 at left and 22 below.
notes: St. Lukes Place is today's Saint Lukes Place; Hillside is today's Hillside Avenue.
The sheet is split along the railroad: this part is 100 feet to an inch (about 4.0 pixels per foot), part 1 is 50 feet.
Hillside Avenue at its foot joins Orange Road and Church Street at one junction.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the top, and covers the civic and commercial centre of the Orange Road district. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally from upper left to right, with Orange Avenue running south from it down the left centre, and Valley Road running south from it along the right. The Bloomfield Avenue frontage is built up with stores and dwellings, including a pool room, a garage and repair shop, a restaurant, a saloon and several shops, and a triangle of land at Bell Street. Between Orange Avenue and Valley Road, block 2 holds a mix of commercial uses: an auto repairing works, storage buildings, a paint shop, a tin and sheet metal shop, a livery stable run by S. Olsson, hardware, plumbing and tinning shops and a large pink (brick) store at the Valley Road corner. South of these are the Central Manual Training School, with its school of cooking, clay modelling, engineering and carpentry, and the Central Primary and Central Grammar Schools, all drawn in pink. On the left, between Saint Lukes Place and Orange Avenue, are rows of small dwellings, and block 1 at lower left holds the Montclair High School with its gymnasium, drawn in pink and blue. Hillside Avenue and Church run across the foot, and the scale bar is lettered "Scale of Feet". Neighbouring sheets are cited as 39 and 37 above, 24 at right and 21 at left and below.
notes: Orange Avenue is today's Orange Road; St. Lukes Place is today's Saint Lukes Place.
Church Street at the lower right is now a roundabout (Church Plaza) and was not used for control.
Only four control points were available: two detected (Bell Street / Bloomfield Avenue / Orange Road; Church / Hillside / Orange Road) and two hand picked from lettered water pipe crossings.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers a residential district of central Montclair south of Bloomfield Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the right of the page. Orange Road runs along the top of the sheet, with Harrison Avenue leaving it at the upper left corner, and South Fullerton Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom. Union runs down the left side, Plymouth down the middle, and Trinity branches east from Plymouth towards The Crescent, which curves along the right side. A short street, Russell Terrace, enters Union from the left. Most of the ground is open: a very large undivided block between Union and Plymouth holds a single dwelling in course of erection and a few detached frame houses and stables at its lower edge, and the block above it is nearly empty apart from three or four dwellings along Orange Road. The strongest development is the row of detached two and a half storey frame dwellings with lots running back from Plymouth and The Crescent, closed at the bottom by the First Congregational Church, a large brick-and-frame building with a spire, shown in blue. Water mains, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets, and widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at the corners. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 17 above Orange Road, 21 beyond Trinity, 18 left of Union, 24 beyond The Crescent and 25 below South Fullerton Avenue.
notes: Printed Union, Plymouth, Trinity and S. Fullerton Av. are today's Union Street, Plymouth Street, Trinity Place and South Fullerton Avenue.
Bradford is cut by the sheet edge and its suffix cannot be read here; it appears as Bradford Pl. on sheet 24.
Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (bar 0 to 150 feet).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 shows the heart of Montclair's business district along Bloomfield Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up the page. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the sheet from the upper left to the lower right, lined on its south-west side by a nearly continuous row of two and three storey stores: groceries, drug stores, a bakery, tobacconists, laundries, shops, the Mansion House at the upper left, Siglers Hotel, a Y.M.C.A. building with gymnasium and bowling alleys, and at the lower end two large blocks shown in pink. Midland Avenue and Park Street enter from the north side, with Maple Place between them. Church runs parallel to Bloomfield Avenue behind the stores, past the Chapel and the First Presbyterian Church at its lower end. On its far side stand residential blocks of detached frame dwellings, with Trinity and Valley Road on the left and Bradford Place in the middle. At the left edge are the Swedish Church, Unity Church (Unitarian) and the Montclair Free Public Library, a Carnegie gift of 1904 with a semicircular plan. At the lower right stand The Montclair Club Inc., with its hall and stage, a row of shops facing South Fullerton Avenue, and a small reading room. The Crescent runs along the bottom of the sheet. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 37 above, 33 across Bloomfield Avenue, 21 and 2 on the left, 23 below and 25 at the right.
notes: Printed Church is today's Church Street; Trinity is Trinity Place; Midland Av. is Midland Avenue.
Maple Place and Bradford Place are not in the modern street data.
A street name at the lower left ending in 'tle Av.' could not be read and is left out.
Control was placed from the edges of Bloomfield Avenue, which is drawn 80 feet wide; the street centre is 40 feet inside the drawn north edge.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 continues Montclair's Bloomfield Avenue business street to the south-east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the top right. Bloomfield Avenue crosses from the upper left to the middle right. Its north-east side carries stores in the first blocks beyond Church: the Crane Building, Morris Building, Times Building and Kirby Building at the left, then groceries, tailors, laundries, a livery stable and the H. J. Koehler Garage in the next block, with Glen Ridge Avenue running along the top of the sheet. The south-west side is mostly large detached dwellings and a boarding house on deep lots, with the First Baptist Church (pink) at the upper left. South Fullerton Avenue runs down the left side and South Willow down the right, crossing Roosevelt Place near the bottom; North Willow leaves Bloomfield Avenue to the north-east. Plymouth Street and The Crescent enter from the left. Below Roosevelt Place are two blocks of frame dwellings, with one large tile-roofed residence in blue at the lower left. Union runs along the bottom edge. Adjoining sheets are numbered 34 above, 24 and 23 on the left, 26 on the right and 18 below.
notes: Printed Glen Ridge Av. is today's Glenridge Avenue; N. and S. Willow are North Willow Street and South Willow Street.
The Bloomfield Avenue and Willow junction is drawn about 5 m from the modern node and was left out of the control.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the Montclair railroad station district and the lower end of Bloomfield Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the top left. Bloomfield Avenue crosses from left to right, with Gates Avenue running south from it near the middle, Greenwood Avenue and Spring running north-west from it, and Grove and Elm along the right edge. North and South Willow bound the left side. Glen Ridge Avenue runs along the top. The upper right is occupied by the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch: Montclair Station with its baggage and waiting rooms, a roundhouse turntable and locomotive house, a freight house with platforms, and many yard tracks. Toney's brook is shown running through it. The Montclair Station area also holds W. O. Persons' lumber, coal and masons' materials yard and the J. D. Mockridge carriage factory. On Bloomfield Avenue are the Crawford Block, Frank E. Clayton's livery stable, the New York and New Jersey Telephone Company central office, Mullens storage warehouse and boarding stable, and St. Paul's Baptist Church (coloured). Ashland Hall stands on the south side. Detached dwellings fill the blocks south of Bloomfield Avenue, with Union along the bottom and Roosevelt Place near the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 31 above, 27 at the right, 15 right of the bottom, 18 below and 25 on the left.
notes: Spring is gone; Lackawanna Plaza now runs near it. Greenwood Avenue is Greenwood Avenue today.
The Montclair Branch passages are rebuilt today (Lackawanna Plaza, Bay Street station).

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 lies north-east of the station district on the Montclair Branch of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Bloomfield Avenue runs down the left side, with Elm and Grove leading off to the north-east, and Glen Ridge Avenue runs down the right side. The railroad's several tracks run north to south through the middle of the sheet, and Toney's Brook crosses from top left to bottom right, bridged where it meets the road and track. West of the tracks are lines of small detached dwellings on Cherry, and larger lots along Bloomfield Avenue, with the New York Hotel, flats, a barber, cobbler, meat market and grocery near Hartley. The Harrison Milling Company mill and the H. O. Dabney coal and wood yard stand beside the brook and the tracks at the top, and J. Blundel and Son coal and wood stand on the east side of the tracks. East of the tracks are dwellings on Glen Ridge Avenue and the First Italian Presbyterian Church. Pine crosses the bottom of the sheet. Clover Hill Place enters Glen Ridge Avenue from the right. Adjoining sheets are 26 above, 15 and 16 on the left, 28 below and 30 on the right.
notes: Printed Glen Ridge Av. is today's Glenridge Avenue.
Pine was realigned: the modern Pine Street does not follow the drawn line, so it was left out of the control.
Clover Hill Place is not in the modern street data.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the south-eastern edge of Montclair's built-up area at the Glen Ridge borough line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Bloomfield Avenue runs down the left side, with New Street, Mission Place and Maple Avenue joining it from the west. The Montclair Branch of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right with Cherry and Pine at the top. Toney's Brook winds across the lower half. Bay Street curves between rows of dwellings and tenements to Glen Ridge Avenue at the right, where the brook passes beneath the road. Baldwin leaves Glen Ridge Avenue to the east. At the upper left are a saloon, a bakery, a row of tenements and a block of flats. S. S. Middleton's coal and wood yard and Henry Lehrmann's coal and wood yard stand by the tracks. The lower right is largely open land with scattered dwellings along Glen Ridge Avenue, and the boundary of Essex County Volume Two and of the Glen Ridge borough crosses the lower part of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are 27 above, 16 and 14 on the left, 30 on the right and Volume Two to the south.
notes: Printed Glen Ridge Av. is today's Glenridge Avenue; Bay is Bay Street; Baldwin is Baldwin Street.
Mission Place is not in the modern street data.
The drawn Pine at the top is not the modern Pine Street, which runs on a different line.
Control includes two hand-picked junctions (Bloomfield Avenue / Maple Avenue and Glenridge Avenue / Bay Street) because the detector could not read their arms.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the south-eastern edge of Montclair against the Glen Ridge borough line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Chestnut runs across the top of the sheet, with Montclair Av. along the left side and Christopher and Grove running down the page in parallel, Grove bending towards the upper right as it leaves the sheet. Oxford crosses the lower right and runs east to the borough boundary; Walnut forms the lower edge, with Walnut Crescent curving round the south-east corner and Pine St. leaving it at the foot of the sheet. The dash-dot line at the right is lettered as the Glen Ridge borough line and as the limit of Essex Co. Vol. Two. West of Christopher the blocks hold a regular row of detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, and a smaller group of houses stands on Oxford and Walnut below a poultry yard and a building with a water tank in the attic supplying several houses. A manufacturer of toilet mirrors is lettered on Oxford. At the left edge a blue stone yard (Thos. Wood) and the Erie Railroad lie beside a pink-coloured building with coal pockets and elevators near the foot of Christopher. Most of the upper right of the sheet, east of Grove and numbered block 4, is open land with no buildings, and a compass is drawn in it. A larger frame building stands at the extreme lower right across the borough line. Water pipes and hydrants are shown in the streets. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 14 to the left, 43 at the lower left, 46 above, 32 and 30 below.
notes: Montclair Av., Chestnut, Christopher, Grove, Oxford, Walnut and Walnut Crescent are today's Montclair Avenue, Chestnut Street, Christopher Street, Grove Street, Oxford Street, Walnut Street and Walnut Crescent; Pine St. runs on as Pine Street on sheet 30.
A curving street lettered ...aremont Av. at the foot of the sheet is cut by the margin, so only the end of its name can be read; it is today's Claremont Avenue.
Oxford Street is drawn only east of Grove on this sheet.
The Erie Railroad at the left edge is on the Greenwood Lake Division; the modern railroad data were not used for this part.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the south-eastern corner of Montclair against the Glen Ridge borough line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Walnut runs along the top with Walnut Crescent curving down from it on the right; Grove forms the left edge and Clairmont runs east from Grove. Pine runs south through the middle to Glen Ridge Av., which crosses the lower part of the sheet from left to right and continues to the lower right. Clover Hill Pl. lies between Grove and Pine. In the lower right Sherman, Grant, Bay, Sherwood, George, Highland Av. and Baldwin are laid out in smaller blocks with closely set houses, flats and tenements, and Bay St. leaves the junction with Glen Ridge Av. towards sheet 28. A multiple-track railroad, lettered Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Div., crosses the sheet diagonally from upper left to lower right. Beside it near Clairmont stand a brass works (Geo. Rutledge), a coal and wood yard (Wm. M. Taylor) and a sash, door and blind factory with planing mill (John T. Lyman). Mountainside Hospital occupies a large block near George and Highland Av., with fire alarm boxes nearby, and a large building with a blue-coloured roof stands near the borough line at the upper right The dash-dot line near the right edge is lettered Glen Ridge Borough and Essex Co. Vol. Two. West of Pine the blocks hold detached dwellings, many on deep lots. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 29 above, 32 and 31 to the left, 27 and 28 below.
notes: Clairmont is today's Claremont Avenue; Clover Hill Pl. is Cloverhill Place; Glen Ridge Av. is Glenridge Avenue; the other streets keep their names with the modern suffix (Walnut Street, Grove Street, Pine Street, Sherman Street, Grant Street, Bay Street, Sherwood Street, George Street, Baldwin Street).
Walnut, Walnut Crescent and Pine have the same names today; the modern railroad line (Montclair line) lies away from the drawn Erie tracks and was not used.
The part rests on 19 control points; Sherwood and the Highland Avenue end of George show the largest residuals (about 4 to 5 m).

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers a block of north-central Montclair bounded by N. Willow along the top, Clairmont Av. on the right, Grove along the foot and Glen Ridge Av. on the left, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Greenwood Av. crosses the sheet from left to right and divides it into block 1 above and block 2 below. A brook is drawn along the upper left corner, and another reach crosses Glen Ridge Av. at the left and runs east through the middle of the lower block. Above Greenwood Av. a row of detached dwellings faces N. Willow, Clairmont Av. and Greenwood Av., and the large pink building of Bordens Condensed Milk Co., Montclair Branch, stands at the left end of Greenwood Av. with wagon, feed, milk and locker rooms and an office. Below Greenwood Av. more dwellings and flats face Clairmont Av. and Glen Ridge Av., and the Fairfield Dairy Stables, with wagon house, sheds and workshop, occupy the lower left. Spring St., a short street lettered at the left margin, leaves Glen Ridge Av. beside the brook. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown in the streets, and street widths of 50 to 66 feet are lettered. A compass at the upper left of the block gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 34 above, 26 to the left, 32 to the right and 30 below.
notes: Clairmont Av. is today's Claremont Avenue and Glen Ridge Av. is Glenridge Avenue; N. Willow is North Willow Street, Greenwood Av. is Greenwood Avenue and Grove is Grove Street.
Spring St. no longer exists as a street in the modern data (compare sheet 26).
The drawn scale (Scale of Feet, 150 feet) matches the fitted pixel scale of about 7.98 pixels per foot.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the Greenwood Av. district of north-central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. N. Willow runs along the top, Clairmont Av. down the left edge, Walnut down the right edge and Grove along the foot, with Greenwood Av. crossing the middle from left to right and Willard Pl. running south from it. A brook runs from the left side of the upper block to N. Willow. West of Willard Pl. a block of detached frame dwellings faces Clairmont Av. On the right side the sheet is industrial: No. 5 Fire House (shown as being built from plans) and Hose Co. No. 5 stand near N. Willow, with A. E. Kinnan and Son livery, the Home Laundry Co., a real estate office, Harold P. Brown Manf., John S. and L. Carlson Co. (planing mill and wood turning), L. Newton Rodgers Lumber Co. and J. H. Connor Coal Co. grouped between Greenwood Av. and the railroad. Several coal and lumber sheds and a water tank serve them. A multiple-track railroad crosses the lower right diagonally with a compass drawn in the triangle it forms with Grove and Walnut. Christopher St. leaves Walnut at the right, and Frinck St. and Erie St. are lettered beyond Walnut at the upper right. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are given throughout. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 36 above, 31 to the left, 43 to the right, 29 at the lower right and 30 below.
notes: Clairmont Av. is today's Claremont Avenue; N. Willow is North Willow Street, Greenwood Av. is Greenwood Avenue, Walnut is Walnut Street (here the north-south stretch), Grove is Grove Street.
Frinck St. is not found under that name in the modern street data; Erie Street exists but meets none of the listed streets.
The modern railroad line lies away from the drawn tracks and was left out of the control points (use_railroads false).

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers four blocks of central Montclair between Clairmont Av. along the top and Bloomfield Av. along the foot, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Midland Av. forms the left edge, Park runs down the middle of the sheet and Cottage Pl. and Fullerton Av. lie on the right, with Munn crossing the right half from Park to Fullerton Av. Montague Pl. and Portland Pl. run across the left half, and Maple Pl. leaves Portland Pl. towards Bloomfield Av. The upper left blocks hold rows of detached frame dwellings on narrow lots with garages and stables behind. On the right, Tegakwitha Hall Parochial School stands with its Amusement Hall, which has bowling alleys and a stage, and a garage and repair shop; below Munn the large pink Church of the Immaculate Conception (Roman Catholic) is shown, its basement used for church purposes while the church is to be built, and the First M.E. Church and its Sunday School stand beside a compass. The blocks along Bloomfield Av. at the foot of the sheet are a continuous row of stores and flats, among them a cleaning and dyeing shop, a plumbing and tin shop and a hall. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are given throughout. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 35 above, 38 to the left, 37 at the lower left, 34 to the right and 24 below.
notes: Clairmont Av. is today's Claremont Avenue; Park is Park Street, Munn is Munn Street and N. Fullerton Av. is North Fullerton Avenue.
Maple Pl. survives only as a service road in the modern data and was not used as control.
The Church of the Immaculate Conception is shown as to be built, with the basement in use.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers a long north-south strip of central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Clairmont Av. runs along the top, N. Fullerton Av. along the left edge and N. Willow along the right edge, with Forest running down the middle. Glen Ridge Av. crosses the foot of the sheet from lower left to right, meeting Bloomfield Av. at the lower left corner, and Munn St. enters from the left margin. A brook crosses the lower part of the sheet from the right edge to the left, passing through Forest and ending near Glen Ridge Av. above the church; the compass stands at the lower right. The upper blocks hold detached frame dwellings, mostly of two and a half storeys, standing on deep lots between N. Fullerton Av., Forest and N. Willow, with a row of semi-detached houses on the right facing Clairmont Av. A large florist's range of greenhouses (A. S. Wallace, Florist, heated by steam and hot water) lies near the left edge below the middle. In the lower left, along Glen Ridge Av. and Bloomfield Av., the blocks hold stores, a printing and tin shop, jewellers and a pink-coloured frame block, with the Swedish Evangelical Lutheran Church on Glen Ridge Av. Water pipes, hydrants and the widths of the streets are lettered throughout. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 36 above, 33 to the left, 31 to the right and 25 below.
notes: Clairmont Av. is today's Claremont Avenue; Glen Ridge Av. is Glenridge Avenue; N. Fullerton Av. is North Fullerton Avenue; N. Willow is North Willow Street; Forest is Forest Street; Munn St. is Munn Street.
Two of the six control points (Forest Street / Glenridge Avenue and Munn Street / North Fullerton Avenue) were hand-picked because the detector found no junction there.
The lower left corner at Bloomfield Av. lies at the sheet edge, so that junction was not used.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 covers two residential blocks in central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, bounded by Midland Avenue along the top of the sheet, Walnut on the right, North Fullerton Avenue along the bottom and Clairmont Avenue on the left; Park runs across the middle and divides the sheet into block 1 above and block 2 below. The sheet is drawn with north towards the upper right. Both blocks are given over almost entirely to large detached frame dwellings, most of two and a half storeys, set back on deep lots, with a scattering of private stables and outbuildings behind them and a few houses with verandas and bay windows. The interior of block 1 is largely open garden ground, and the lower block has a row of smaller dwellings facing North Fullerton Avenue and a short row of houses on the Clairmont Avenue side. Cottage Place, a short street lettered on the left margin, leads off Clairmont Avenue towards the adjoining sheet. Street widths are lettered at the corners (66 feet on Midland Avenue, 50 to 60 feet elsewhere), house numbers run along each frontage, and water pipes with their sizes and the positions of hydrants are shown in every street. There are no commercial, industrial or public buildings on the sheet. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 38 above Midland Avenue, 41 beyond Walnut, 36 below North Fullerton Avenue and 33 beyond Clairmont Avenue.
notes: Clairmont Avenue is today's Claremont Avenue.
Park is today's Park Street; Walnut is today's Walnut Street.
50 ft. Pilot. Midland Av, Park, N. Fullerton Av, Clairmont Av (= Claremont Avenue), Walnut.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers the blocks between N. Fullerton Av. and N. Willow in north-central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. N. Fullerton Av. runs across the top, Clairmont Av. down the left edge and Walnut down the right edge, with N. Willow along the foot. Forest crosses the middle of the sheet from the lower left to Walnut, dividing it into block 1 above and block 2 below. A brook enters from the lower left, passes the compass at N. Willow and crosses the right half of the sheet before reaching Walnut. Above Forest the blocks hold detached frame dwellings on deep lots, some with stables. At the right end of Forest stand Booth's Block, a three-storey block of flats and stores shown in blue, with a fire alarm box beside it, and the Odd Fellows Hall. Below Forest the dwellings stand in a long row along the street and another row faces Clairmont Av. on the left, while the southern part of the sheet beside the brook is open land with a few small outbuildings. Frinck St. and Erie St. are lettered at the right margin beyond Walnut. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are lettered throughout. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 35 above, 34 to the left, 43 to the right and 32 below.
notes: Clairmont Av. is today's Claremont Avenue; N. Fullerton Av. is North Fullerton Avenue; Forest is Forest Street; Walnut is Walnut Street; N. Willow is North Willow Street.
Frinck St. is not found under that name in the modern street data.
Booth's Block is lettered on the sheet.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers the western edge of the central business district of Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Bloomfield Avenue runs up the left side and meets Midland Avenue at the lower left, while the broad diagonal of Valley Road crosses the middle of the sheet from lower left to upper right. Along the top, Bell Street and a short Mount View Place bound the block to the north. The largest feature is the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey's Montclair car barn and power house, a long pink brick and fireproof structure with a lettered note listing its watchman, steam heat, electric light, sprinklers and fire-hose equipment. Along Bloomfield Avenue below it are Leach's storage house, a Montclair van company, the Montclair auto station, Fire House Hose and Truck Company No. 1, the police station, a laundry, and a cluster of livery, carriage and paint shops near Midland Avenue, including the J. W. Van Gieson livery. Union Baptist Church stands between Valley Road and Midland Avenue. The right half of the sheet is a residential district of detached frame dwellings with stables and sheds, laid out on narrow lots along Portland Place and Montague Place, with a stair builder's shop beside the latter. Pipe sizes, hydrants and street widths are lettered in every street, and the neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 39 above, 38 to the right, 33 below and 22 and 24 to the left.
notes: Orange Av. is today's Orange Road; Valley is today's Valley Road; Mt View Pl. is today's Mountain View Place.
The car barn and power house of the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey occupy the block between Bell and Valley Road.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows a residential section of central Montclair at 50 feet to an inch, bounded by Midland Avenue along the foot of the sheet, Montague Place on the left and Walnut on the right, with Valley Road and Bell cutting across the top left corner. Clairmont Avenue runs up the middle of the sheet from Midland Avenue towards Valley Road, and Vincent Place crosses it near the lower third to join Walnut. The area is almost entirely detached frame dwellings, mostly two and a half storeys, on deep lots; a row of near-identical houses fronts the east side of Montague Place and a shorter row of dwellings with barns faces Vincent Place and Midland Avenue. The only public building is Trinity Presbyterian Church with its chapel, shown in blue at the corner of Midland and Clairmont Avenues. A large undivided lot marked 1 fills the interior between Montague Place and Clairmont Avenue and is left blank. Street widths are lettered at 50 and 66 feet, and water pipe sizes and hydrants appear in each street. The compass at the top shows north towards the upper right. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 39 above, 37 to the left, 40 to the right and 35 and 33 below, and Central Avenue is lettered at the right edge.
notes: Clairmont Avenue is today's Claremont Avenue; Walnut is today's Walnut Street; Valley is today's Valley Road.
Reading made from a full-sheet view at reduced scale and not from 1:1 crops; lettering of small labels may be incomplete.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers a residential block on the north-west side of central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Unlike most neighbouring sheets, north points towards the upper left, with the compass at the left margin. N. Mountain Avenue runs down the left side, Clairmont Avenue bounds the top, Bloomfield Avenue crosses the bottom, and Valley Road and Bell run down the right side. Between them Mount View Place and Francis Place are laid out as short streets within the block. The buildings are almost all large detached frame dwellings of two and a half storeys, many with stables and outbuildings, set well back on deep lots; the middle of the block and the area around Francis Place are largely open garden ground. There are no commercial or industrial buildings. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and street widths (30 to 80 feet) are lettered in each street, and a fire alarm box stands on N. Mountain Avenue near Bloomfield Avenue. South Mountain Avenue and Saint Lukes Place are lettered where they leave Bloomfield Avenue at the bottom. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 40 above, 38 and 37 to the right, 22 below right, 21 below and 19 to the left.
notes: Clairmont Avenue is today's Claremont Avenue; Mt. View Pl. is today's Mountain View Place; Orange Avenue is today's Orange Road.
The sheet is turned: north is towards the upper left, unlike sheets 37, 38 and 41 to 43.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, unlike its 50 foot neighbours, and takes in the district north of Walnut around the point where Valley Road, Central Avenue and James Street meet, in the northern part of central Montclair. The compass puts north towards the upper left. Along the left side runs N. Mountain Avenue with Alpine Street and Club Street at the top and Van Vleck Street branching off it; Valley Road follows a diagonal from the top left to Clairmont Avenue at the bottom. Central Avenue and Midland Avenue form the right side, with Chestnut and James Streets crossing the sheet east to west, and Bellair Drive and Belvidere Road in the upper left. Walnut runs along the bottom. The densest development is a small grid of narrow lots around William, Dey and Talbot streets in the middle, with small dwellings, shops and sheds; the rest is scattered houses on larger lots, and the upper part of the sheet is open land. A strip marked as railroad right of way crosses diagonally between Valley Road and James Street. Street widths of 50 to 66 feet are lettered, together with water pipes and hydrants. The adjoining sheets are 49 above, 42 and 41 to the right, 38 and 39 below, and 51 and 20 to the left.
notes: Printed at 100 feet to an inch; the fitted scale of 3.94 pixels per foot agrees.
Belvidere Road is today's Belvidere Place; Clairmont Avenue is today's Claremont Avenue; Bellair Drive is today's Bellaire Drive.
Reading made from a full-sheet view at reduced scale; some small lettering in the William, Dey and Talbot streets block may be missing.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows two long residential blocks of central Montclair at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. Midland Avenue forms the top of the sheet, Park runs across the middle, and N. Fullerton Avenue is along the bottom; Walnut bounds the left and James the right. A short Walnut Place leads off N. Fullerton Avenue in the lower middle. The upper block between Midland Avenue and Park is lined with detached frame dwellings, mostly two and a half storeys, on narrow lots running back from Midland Avenue, with a few stables and sheds along a rear lot line, and some small outbuildings in the right-hand part. The lower block between Park and N. Fullerton Avenue has dwellings facing Walnut and a row of double houses along Walnut Place, with the central part left as open lots. There are no commercial or industrial buildings. Street widths of 60 and 66 feet and water pipes are lettered at the corners. The neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 40 above, 35 to the left, 42 to the right, 43 below left and 44 below right.
notes: Walnut is today's Walnut Street and Park is today's Park Street.
Reading made from a full-sheet view at reduced scale.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 shows residential blocks east of Walnut Place at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right and a compass in the blank upper left. Midland Avenue crosses the top, Park runs across the middle and N. Fullerton Avenue the bottom; James is lettered on the left side of the built-up area and Chestnut runs down the right edge. The left third of the sheet above Park is blank, belonging to the neighbouring sheet 41. Dwellings stand in three groups: a block between James, Chestnut and Park at the upper right, a long row of detached frame houses with outbuildings along the north side of Park, and a short run of houses at Walnut Place at the lower left. Most of the land between Park and N. Fullerton Avenue is open lots divided by property lines. There are no commercial or industrial buildings. Street widths of 60 and 66 feet and water pipes are lettered. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 40 above, 41 to the left, 49 and 48 to the right and 44 below.
notes: Chestnut is today's Chestnut Street; Park is today's Park Street.
Reading made from a full-sheet view at reduced scale.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 covers the Montclair manufacturing district around the United States Printing Company works, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. N. Fullerton Avenue runs along the top, Walnut down the left side, and Forest across the upper middle; below Forest the sheet shows Label, Frink, Erie and Oak Place. The top of the sheet is residential, with detached dwellings along Friendship Place and Fidelity Place. The centre is occupied by the large pink brick works of the United States Printing Company, with its coating branch, mixing, storage, cutting and finishing and shipping departments, sprinklers and its own railroad spur, and a lettered note on the right gives its fire protection. Beside it are Montclair Jam Kitchens (H. Dodge and Company) and a lot of dwellings between Walnut and Label; a stream crosses the sheet in blue, one branch to the left of Label and another curving through the right side. At the lower left on Walnut are shops and flats, and along the bottom the Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division runs diagonally with a freight house, an express office and the iron-clad depot. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 41 and 42 above, 36 and 32 to the left, 44 to the right and 14 and 29 below.
notes: Fidelity Place meets Forest and Oak Place about 9 m from the modern node and was left out of the fit.
Friendship Place north of Forest continues as Label to the south on the sheet; modern data has two nearby junctions.
Reading made from a full-sheet view at reduced scale; the Erie Railroad is not used as control.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 lies on the north-east side of central Montclair, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. North Fullerton Avenue runs across the top of the sheet, Forest across the middle and Chestnut down the right-hand side; Fidelity Place and Oak Place run down the left, with Sylvan Place between them and the centre of the sheet, and Erie closes the block at the bottom against the Erie Railroad. A brook crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right, passing under Forest and running through the back lots of the block above it. The block between North Fullerton Avenue and Forest is lined with detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, most of two and a half storeys, with the Chestnut Street Public School, a large brick building marked as a manual training school, standing near its right-hand end. The block below Forest holds more dwellings facing Sylvan Place and Oak Place, and Grace Presbyterian Church stands on the Chestnut side. The lower part of the sheet is taken up by the double track of the Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, which crosses diagonally from lower left to upper right, with sidings on the near side. Street widths are lettered at the corners (60 and 66 feet on the main streets, 40 and 50 feet on the places), water pipes are shown in the streets, and a compass at the left gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are named in the margins: 42 above, 43 to the left, 48 to the right and 14 below.
notes: The printed scale is 'Scale of Feet' with 50 and 100 foot divisions, taken as 50 feet to an inch; the fit gives 8.0 px per foot.

Forest, Chestnut, Fidelity Place, Oak Place and Sylvan Place keep their printed names today as Forest Street, Chestnut Street, Fidelity Place, Oak Place and Sylvan Place; North Fullerton Avenue is unchanged.
Walnut Place is lettered at the upper left edge and Essex Street at the lower right edge, both belonging mainly to adjoining sheets.
The junction of Oak Place with Forest and Fidelity Place was left out of the fit: today's street lies about 7 metres east of the drawn line.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 covers the north-eastern edge of Montclair against the Glen Ridge borough line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Watchung Avenue crosses the top of the sheet and McDonough and Dodd the bottom. Montclair Avenue runs down the left side, with Christopher and Grove streets parallel to it across the middle. The ground is mostly open: large unbuilt tracts divided by long property lines, with a handful of detached dwellings and outbuildings scattered along Montclair Avenue and Grove. A larger frame house named Marlboro House stands in the block between Christopher and Grove close to Watchung Avenue, with its stable and a cottage beside it. A row of small narrow lots with detached dwellings lines both sides of Gray, which branches from Grove on the right and runs towards the borough line. Fairfield and Frederick meet Montclair Avenue from the left edge, drawn as short stubs belonging mainly to sheet 47. The right edge of the sheet is the Glen Ridge borough boundary, lettered with the volume reference to Essex County Volume Two. Water pipes with sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown in the streets, and a compass at upper left gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are given by number: 57 above, 47 to the left and 46 below.
notes: Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.98 px per foot.
Montclair Avenue is lettered both on the vertical street and on a short branch at the upper left.
