Grove, Gray, Dodd and McDonough keep their printed names today as Grove Street, Gray Street, Dodd Street and McDonough Street.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 lies on the north-eastern edge of Montclair beside the Glen Ridge borough line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. McDonough and Dodd cross the top of the sheet, with Montclair Avenue, Christopher and Grove running down it as three parallel streets, and Columbus Avenue crossing near the bottom. Chestnut closes the sheet at the lower edge. Most of the sheet is open ground divided into large tracts, with a few houses and outbuildings. Built-up frontage is confined to the lower left, where small detached dwellings line Montclair Avenue and Christopher on lots about 50 feet wide on both sides of Columbus Avenue, and St. Johns Episcopal Church stands near the corner of Chestnut and Montclair Avenue. On the right, a long strip of land between Grove and the borough line has a farmhouse group with a lane, a larger dwelling and a pink-coloured building near the bottom of the strip. The right edge of the sheet is the boundary of Glen Ridge Borough, lettered with the reference to Essex County Volume Two. Street widths (50, 60 and 66 feet) are lettered, water pipes are shown in the streets, and a compass at the left gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 45 above, 48 to the left and 29 below.
notes: Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.99 px per foot.
McDonough, Dodd, Christopher, Grove and Chestnut keep their printed names today as McDonough Street, Dodd Street, Christopher Street, Grove Street and Chestnut Street.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers a residential district in north-eastern Montclair around the Watchung station, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Watchung Avenue crosses the top and McDonough the bottom; N. Fullerton Avenue and Montclair Avenue run down the sheet, the latter along the right edge, with Essex Avenue between them. Fairfield, Garden and Frederick cross between N. Fullerton and Montclair Avenue, and an unnamed street is lettered 'Street No Name' below Frederick. Along Watchung Avenue are the Watchung Congregational Church and rows of detached frame dwellings, and the Watchung Public School stands on the block between Garden and Frederick. The lower blocks, numbered 6 to 8, are almost empty. Down the left side the double track of the Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, runs from top to bottom, with a small station labelled Park Street Station near its upper end and Park running parallel on its west side. Waterbury Road is lettered at the top between Watchung Avenue and the sheet edge. Water pipes with sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown in the streets, and a compass at the right gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 56 above, 50 to the left, 45 to the right, and 48 and 49 below.
notes: Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.98 px per foot.
Waterbury Road is lettered at the top edge and is not in today's street network.
'Street No Name' is a street lettered without a name between Frederick and McDonough; it corresponds to no named modern street.
Park, Fairfield, Garden, Frederick and McDonough keep their printed names today as Park Street, Fairfield Street, Garden Street, Frederick Street and McDonough Street.
The Park Street station text is partly hidden by the railroad lines and was read with low confidence.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 lies along the Erie Railroad in north-eastern Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Chestnut runs down the left edge. Park crosses the top, and N. Fullerton Avenue runs across the upper part from Chestnut to the right, with Forest below it near the left edge. Essex and Montclair Avenue cross the lower part, Columbus Avenue runs between them and McDonough forms the right-hand margin. The double track of the Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right, dividing the block between N. Fullerton Avenue and Essex. Dwellings on narrow lots lie at the left in the triangle between Chestnut, Forest and the railroad, and a long row of small houses faces Montclair Avenue at the bottom left. Park, at the top, carries a few detached dwellings on large lots. Most of the area right of Columbus Avenue is open, with a strip of narrow platted lots, marked as a right of way, running down towards Montclair Avenue. Street widths (50, 60 and 66 feet) are lettered, water pipes are shown in the streets, and a compass at the top gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 49 above, 42 and 44 on the left, 47 on the right and 46 below.
notes: Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.95 px per foot.
North Fullerton Avenue is lettered twice, along the upper street and on the diagonal street at the right.
Essex Street lettered at the right edge is a separate lettering from Essex between Chestnut and Columbus Avenue and belongs mainly to the adjoining sheet.
Park, Chestnut, Forest, Essex, McDonough and Columbus Avenue keep their printed names today as Park Street, Chestnut Street, Forest Street, Essex Avenue, McDonough Street and Columbus Avenue.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers an upper-class residential district of central Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. N. Mountain Avenue runs across the top and Valley Road crosses below it, running down towards the lower right; Central Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet and Midland Avenue the lower part, with Park along the bottom edge. Chestnut runs down the left edge. Club, Bellair Drive and Belvidere Road lie between Chestnut and the centre. The Montclair Athletic Club and its athletic field occupy the large block between Valley Road and Central Avenue; its buildings, drawn at the top of the field, include a squash court and a bowling alley. At the right, Erwin Park, a residential tract of curving roads laid out in loops, with Erwin Park Way and Erwin Park Road, holds detached frame dwellings on large lots. Chestnut and Midland Avenue carry rows of detached dwellings on narrow lots, and long curved property lines cross the large blocks numbered 3 in the middle of the sheet. A compass at the right gives the orientation. Street widths, water pipes with sizes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 51 above, 40 to the left, 50 to the right, and 42 and 48 below.
notes: Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.98 px per foot.
Bellair Drive is today's Bellaire Drive; Belvidere Road is today's Belvidere Place.
Club, Chestnut and Park keep their printed names today as Club Street, Chestnut Street and Park Street.

Erwin Park Way and Erwin Park Road are lettered in pieces along the curving roads; the readings were made on full-resolution crops of the Erwin Park area but the tract name Erwin Park is low confidence.
The junction of Bellair Drive with Central Avenue was left out of the fit (drawn curve does not match the modern node).

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 covers the Erwin Park district in the north-west of central Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Mountain Avenue runs across the top. Valley Road runs from the upper left towards the lower right, ending at Watchung Avenue, which forms the right-hand edge; Central Avenue enters from the left. Midland Avenue crosses the lower part, with Park along the bottom of the sheet. Berkeley Place and Edgemont Road lie at the upper left, with a short stretch of Edgemont Road also lettered at the right edge. The large block between Mountain Avenue and Valley Road, numbered 1, is open ground. Below Valley Road, Erwin Park Road and Holland Terrace cross the district: detached frame dwellings of two and a half storeys stand on large lots along both sides of Holland Terrace, Erwin Park Road and Midland Avenue, with Erwin Park Way curving at the left edge. At the bottom right, the double track of the Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, passes the foot of the sheet. A compass in the upper middle gives the orientation. Street widths, water pipes with sizes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at Watchung Avenue are shown. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 52 above, 49 to the left, 55 to the right, 56 below the right edge and 47 below.
notes: Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.99 px per foot.
Mountain Avenue is lettered without a North; today's street is North Mountain Avenue.
Park keeps its printed name today as Park Street.
The junctions of Watchung Avenue with North Mountain Avenue and with Edgemont Road were left out of the fit; today's Watchung Avenue lies about 8 metres from the drawn line there.
Edgemont Road at the right edge and Park at the foot of the sheet were read at lower resolution.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 covers the north-west corner of Montclair, against the Verona Township line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The sheet is tinted yellow. Highland Avenue crosses the upper middle and Prospect Avenue runs parallel below it. Upper Mountain Avenue lies across the lower middle and N. Mountain Avenue along the foot, with Alpine and Club running down from them at the left, and Berkeley Place down the right edge. Holmes Place and Edgewood Road branch from Highland Avenue towards the lower middle. The upper third of the sheet is open land bounded by the dash-dot line of Verona Township, with a cluster of blue-coloured structures near the township line beside a stream. Crestmont Road runs along the top left. Between Highland and Upper Mountain Avenue detached frame dwellings stand on large lots, with more along Upper Mountain Avenue, and a larger pink-coloured building lies near Holmes Place. Few houses stand below Upper Mountain Avenue. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at Berkeley Place are shown. A compass at the upper right gives the orientation. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 20 to the left, 52 to the right, 40 and 49 below.
notes: Holmes Place north of Edgewood Road is today's Edgewood Terrace, and the stretch from Edgewood Road to Upper Mountain Avenue is today's Edgewood Road.
Alpine keeps its printed name today as Alpine Street; Club Street is unchanged.
The blue-coloured structures near the township line were not identified.

100 ft; scan tinted yellow. Turned (north upper right). Highland Av, Prospect Av, Upper Mountain Av, N. Mountain Av, Holmes Pl (= Edgewood Terrace / Edgewood Road), Edgewood Road, Berkeley Pl, Alpine, Verona Township line.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 lies at the north-west corner of the built-up area of Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The top of the sheet is bounded by the Verona Township line, a dash-dot boundary running across the upper part, and the sheet shows mostly undeveloped land. Two roads cross it: Upper Mountain Avenue and, below it, North Mountain Avenue run from the lower left towards the upper right, both lettered 60 feet wide. Berkeley Place meets them at the lower left, and Watchung Avenue runs down the right-hand edge past both. At the upper left Highland Avenue enters from the left edge and Edgewood Road branches from it at a sharp angle towards the lower left. The land north of Upper Mountain Avenue is divided into very large unbuilt tracts by long property lines, and only a few dwellings stand there, near the avenue. Between Upper Mountain Avenue and North Mountain Avenue are a handful of detached frame dwellings, outbuildings and a pair of long greenhouses near Watchung Avenue. At the top right a rectangular lot carries a water tank, marked 40 feet in diameter and 50 feet high, with a water main running to it. Water mains with their sizes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at Berkeley Place and another at Watchung Avenue are shown. Neighbouring sheets are given by number in the margins: 51 to the left, 53 to the right and 50 below.
notes: Highland Avenue, Edgewood Road and Berkeley Place, Upper Mountain Avenue, North Mountain Avenue and Watchung Avenue keep their printed names today.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch; the fit gives 3.97 px per foot.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 covers a strip of Upper Mountain Avenue and North Mountain Avenue on the western edge of Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The left side of the sheet is the Verona Township line, a heavy dash-dot boundary running down the sheet from top to bottom, with unbuilt land beyond it. Upper Mountain Avenue runs from the bottom of the sheet to the top, lettered 60 feet wide, and North Mountain Avenue runs parallel to it on the right; both meet Watchung Avenue at the foot of the sheet, where a fire alarm box is shown. Brookfield Road enters from the right edge and joins North Mountain Avenue about two thirds of the way down, and a strip labelled Right of Way crosses at the right edge. Between the township line and Upper Mountain Avenue the land is cut into long narrow lots running back from the avenue, and only a few large detached dwellings and their stables, coops and an auto storage building stand on them. Between the two avenues and east of North Mountain Avenue the lots are larger and sparsely built, with a few dwellings, a summer house and coops. At the lower left a small lot on the township line carries a water tank, 40 feet by 30 feet, with 12 inch and 6 inch water pipes leading to it. Hydrants and water mains are lettered along the avenues. The margins give the neighbouring sheets 54 above, 63 and 55 to the right and 52 below.
notes: Brookfield Road is cut off at the right edge of the sheet and is lettered Brookfield R there; the full name is printed on sheet 55.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.
Only three junctions are drawn; the fit is exact through three points and its scale (4.07 px per foot) is about 3 percent above the other 100 ft sheets.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 covers the north-western edge of Montclair around the junction of Upper Mountain Avenue and Bradford Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. North points to the right, so the township line with Verona at the top of the sheet runs along the upper edge as a dash-dot boundary. Van Gieson Gap Road or Bradford Avenue enters from the upper left and curves down to meet Upper Mountain Avenue, which crosses the sheet from the left edge to the lower right; North Mountain Avenue runs below and parallel to it on the left. Edgecliff Road leaves Bradford Avenue to the east, and Highland Avenue runs off it on both sides. Braemore Road runs in a curve from Upper Mountain Avenue up towards Highland Avenue and has a second, east-west stretch below Upper Mountain Avenue. Belleview Avenue and Lorraine Avenue run down the left half of the sheet and Jerome Place down the right. In the lower part the Greenwood Lake Division of the Erie Railroad crosses the sheet in a wide curve, with Valley Road below it and Oakwood, Inwood and Fernwood avenues running south from Valley Road. The area is a district of large detached frame dwellings on deep lots, with long unbuilt tracts between the roads on the left. At the upper right, Osborne and Marsellis Company, contractors, occupy a yard of sheds and a small steam power plant with a 3000 gallon water tank and an elevated platform. Water mains, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown along the avenues. Neighbouring sheets are named in the margins: 53 to the left, 61 to the right, 63 and 64 below.
notes: Belleview Avenue is today's Bellevue Avenue.
The street lettered Van Gieson Gap Road or Bradford Av. is today's Bradford Avenue.
Jerome Place is lettered Jerome south of the railroad and Pl. north of it; the name is read from both.
The Greenwood Lake Division of the Erie Railroad is the present Montclair Line.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.

Highland Avenue is lettered Highland west of Bradford Avenue and Av. to the east; Valley Road junctions east of Lorraine Avenue (Oakwood, Inwood, Jerome Place, Fernwood) were 5 to 7 m off the modern line in a trial and were left out of the fit.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 covers a sparsely built district on the west side of Montclair between North Mountain Avenue and Valley Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. North Mountain Avenue forms the left edge and Watchung Avenue the bottom. Valley Road bounds the right side, curving from the upper left of its stretch to the lower right, and the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division runs diagonally across the upper right of the sheet, drawn as a bundle of parallel lines. Brookfield Road crosses the middle of the sheet from North Mountain Avenue to Valley Road, and Edgemont Road runs north from Watchung Avenue, splitting around a long oval island before it meets Brookfield Road. Appleton Place, Gordon Hurst Avenue and Wildwood Avenue branch off Valley Road on the right, and North Veiw Avenue enters at the top right. A long strip of land labelled Right of Way runs across the upper left, divided into narrow lots on its lower side. Most of the sheet is open ground. Detached frame dwellings, mostly of two and a half storeys, line North Mountain Avenue, Brookfield Road, Edgemont Road and Watchung Avenue, with several small houses on narrow lots along Brookfield Road. The main institution is the Montclair Water Company pumping station in the lower middle, shown as a pink brick building with its engine and pump particulars lettered beside it, a coal pile, an old well and a ring of large water mains around it. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at Valley Road and Watchung Avenue are marked. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 53 on the left, 63 above and to the right, 56 on the right and 50 below.
notes: North Veiw Avenue is lettered with this spelling; it is today's Northview Avenue.
Gordon Hurst Avenue is today's Gordonhurst Avenue.
The Greenwood Lake Division of the Erie Railroad is the present Montclair Line.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.

Edgemont Road and Brookfield Road meet in a pair of curves around an oval island; the modern junction there lies about 4 m from the drawn one. Junctions along Valley Road at Brookfield Road and Gordon Hurst Avenue were not used because the modern Valley Road differs from the drawn line by 6 to 8 m.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers a district of north-western Montclair along Park and North Fullerton Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Wildwood Avenue forms the top of the sheet and Watchung Avenue the bottom, with Valley Road curving down the left side and Waterbury Road along the right edge. Park, running from top to bottom, and North Fullerton Avenue, parallel to it on the right, divide the sheet into long blocks, which are crossed by Gordon Hurst Avenue on the left of Park and Park Place on the right. Valley Road, Brookfield Road and Appleton Place lie at the lower left, where the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division crosses diagonally and a triangular block between the railroad and Valley Road is cut into narrow lots lettered A, B and C along Appleton Place. North View Avenue enters at the top left. Most of the blocks are large and unbuilt, laid out in long strips running back from the streets. The built-up parts are detached frame dwellings, mainly of two and a half storeys, along the west side of Park, along Waterbury Road, the lower end of North Fullerton Avenue and Watchung Avenue, with small groups of houses and stables at the upper right on narrow lots off Wildwood Avenue. A few dwellings carry the note From Plans, meaning they were not yet built when the sheet was drawn. A cluster of outbuildings stands in the middle of the lower Park block. Water pipes of 6 inch to 20 inch, hydrants and the positions of dwelling numbers are shown along the streets. The margins give the neighbouring sheets: 63 and 58 above, 55 and 50 to the left, 57 on the right and 47 below.
notes: Park is today's Park Street.
Gordon Hurst Avenue on the west of Park and Park Place on the east of it together make today's Gordonhurst Avenue.
Midland Avenue is cut off at the bottom edge of the sheet.
The Greenwood Lake Division of the Erie Railroad is the present Montclair Line.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.
Watchung Avenue / Waterbury Road was 4 m off the other control points and was excluded; Park Street / Watchung Avenue and Appleton Place / Valley Road are hand-picked.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 covers the southern edge of Montclair along the Glen Ridge and Bloomfield boundaries, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the right, so streets that run north and south on the ground run across the sheet. Watchung Avenue forms the left edge, with Waterbury Road curving along the top and Montclair Avenue curving across the upper left. Beverly Road runs down the sheet from Montclair Avenue, crossing Christopher and Grove; Park Place, lettered Park below Grove, is the next cross street to the right, and Wildwood Avenue forms the right edge. Grove runs across the whole sheet near the middle and divides it into an upper half of large blocks and a lower half that is mostly open. The sheet is thinly built: a few detached frame dwellings of two and a half storeys stand along Waterbury Road, Beverly Road and Park Place, and a group of dwellings, outbuildings and sheds lies on the east side of Park Place below Grove. Between Montclair Avenue and Christopher the blocks are large and have only a few houses, and a short row of lots near the right edge is cut up by lot lines. A strip near the lower right edge is lettered Division. At the bottom a dash-dot line, lettered Glen Ridge Borough, Essex Co. Vol. Two, and further right Town of Bloomfield, Essex Co. Vol. Two, marks the boundary beyond which the ground is shown on the neighbouring volume. A fire alarm box stands at Watchung Avenue and Grove. Water mains of 6 inch to 20 inch and hydrants are marked. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 47, 56, 58, 45 and 60.
notes: Park Place is lettered Park Pl. north of Grove and Park south of it.
Grove is today's Grove Street and Park Place is today's Gordonhurst Avenue.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.
Christopher / Watchung Avenue was 4 m off the fit and was excluded; Watchung Avenue / Waterbury Road at the corner of the sheet is kept at about 5 m residual.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers a thinly built part of north-western Montclair between Park and Grove, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the right, so streets that run north and south on the ground cross the sheet from side to side. Park runs along the top of the sheet and Grove along the bottom. Wildwood Avenue forms the left edge and Belleview Avenue the right edge, and Summit Avenue and Cooper Avenue run down from Park into the large blocks; Summit Avenue is shown with dashed edges as a street not yet opened. North Fullerton Avenue enters at the left edge about a third of the way down. Most of the ground is open and divided into large lots by property lines. The few buildings are detached frame dwellings of two and a half storeys with their outbuildings: a group of larger houses and stables near the top, between Summit Avenue and Belleview Avenue, a small row of three houses lettered A, B and C on Wildwood Avenue, and scattered dwellings and sheds in the big central block and along Grove at the bottom. Two unnamed cross streets, each lettered No Name, run down the bottom edge from Grove. Water mains with their sizes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at the corner of Park and Belleview Avenue are marked. The neighbouring sheets are named in the margins: 63 above, 56 and 57 on the left, 59 on the right and 60 below.
notes: Park is today's Park Street, Grove is today's Grove Street and Belleview Avenue is today's Bellevue Avenue.
Two unnamed streets at the bottom edge are lettered No Name.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.
Park Street / Summit Avenue was excluded because Summit Avenue is drawn only as a dashed street; Park Street / Bellevue Avenue is kept at about 4 m residual.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 covers a residential district of north-western Montclair between Park and Grove, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the right, so Park runs across the top of the sheet and Grove across the bottom, and the cross streets run down the sheet. From left to right these are Belleview Avenue along the left edge, Lorraine Avenue, Haddon Place, Clairwill Avenue and Inwood Avenue, which curves along the right side and meets Park and Grove at skew angles. The streets are lettered 50 or 60 feet wide. The blocks are filled by detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, mostly on narrow lots with the house numbers marked along the frontage, with a larger group of dwellings and stables on the blocks between Belleview Avenue and Lorraine Avenue and a row of newer houses along the west side of Clairwill Avenue. The two large blocks between Lorraine Avenue and Haddon Place hold only a couple of big houses set in open grounds. Along the top, short rows of dwellings on lots lettered A, B, C, D and E front Park. The area east of Inwood Avenue is blank, belonging to sheet 66. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches, hydrants and two fire alarm boxes, at Belleview Avenue and Park and at Inwood Avenue and Park, are shown. The margins give the neighbouring sheets: 63 and 64 above, 58 on the left, 60 and 66 below and to the right.
notes: Park is today's Park Street, Grove is today's Grove Street, Belleview Avenue is today's Bellevue Avenue and Clairwill Avenue is today's Clarewill Avenue.
Printed scale 100 Ft. to One Inch.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 lies in the north-east corner of Upper Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the Essex County line against the Town of Bloomfield (Volume Two) crossing the sheet as a dash-dot line from the top right to the bottom. Grove runs down the left edge and Belleview Avenue sweeps across the upper part from Grove towards the county line, where it continues as Bellevue Avenue. Between Belleview Avenue and Wildwood Avenue at the bottom, two unnamed 50 foot streets are lettered Street (No Name) and numbered blocks 2 and 3 are laid out in lots along Grove, with Park Place and Division running south to Wildwood Avenue in block 4. The sheet is largely open land. The upper left is the links of the Upper Montclair Country Golf Club, whose club house stands on the north side of Belleview Avenue, and the large area to the east is farmland and unplatted ground with a handful of dwellings, barns and outbuildings, including John Garretson's cider works with its steam power plant. A pond or stream end is coloured blue at the county line. Dwellings are concentrated along Grove and in the lots of the lower left, a few of them stone or plastered, with coops and sheds behind. Water pipe sizes and hydrants are marked in Grove and Belleview Avenue. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 66 above, 59 and 58 to the left and 57 below.
notes: Belleview Avenue is today's Bellevue Avenue; the sheet letters the part east of the county line Bellevue Av.
Grove is today's Grove Street; Lorraine St. is today's Lorraine Avenue.
The two unnamed streets are not in the modern street network.
Placed from three points along Grove Street and one hand-picked point at Division and Wildwood Avenue; low confidence.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 covers the north-western edge of Upper Montclair against Verona Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Upper Mountain Avenue crosses the sheet from the left to the lower right and Valley Road runs along the bottom, with the Erie Railroad (Greenwood Lake Division) between them on a straight embankment and a small station, Mountain Av. R.R. Station, at the right. North of Upper Montclair's main street the ground is mostly unbuilt: long narrow lots run up to the Verona Township line, cut by the paper streets Mountain Place, Valley Place and Montgomery Place, only a few of which carry any buildings. Dwellings of two and a half storeys stand along Upper Mountain Avenue, Norwood Place and Jerome Place, and a row of houses with outbuildings fronts the south side of Valley Road and Laurel Place, together with the greenhouses of Payne and Haas, florists, on Valley Road. At the top left the Osborne and Marsellis Co. quarry is shown with its sheds and rail spurs. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets and a fire alarm box stands at Jerome Place and Laurel Place. Street widths of 40 to 60 feet are lettered. The sheet has a compass at the upper right. Neighbouring sheets are 54 at the left, 62 at the right, 64 and 65 below and 0 above.
notes: Mountain Place north of Upper Mountain Avenue is probably today's Mountain Terrace and Montgomery Place today's Windsor Place (identified from their positions, not from a printed link).
Upper Mountain Avenue / Valley Place was measured 7 m off the fit and left out; the modern Valley Place may not follow the drawn line.
Fernwood Avenue / Valley Road is left out of the fit because its modern junction sits about 4 m from the drawn one.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 shows the northern end of Upper Montclair between the Verona Township line on the left and Valley Road on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Upper Mountain Avenue runs diagonally from Mount Hebron Road at the top to the foot of the sheet, where it meets Laurel Place beside the Erie Railroad (Greenwood Lake Division), whose double main line crosses the sheet roughly parallel to it. Mount Hebron Road crosses the top, with Smith Av. leaving it to the north, and Valley Road bounds the right edge, with Alexander Av., Elston Road, Laurel Pl. and Glenwood Road entering it. The sheet is almost entirely open: the large block 1 west of Upper Mountain Avenue and blocks 2 and 3 between the road, the railroad and Valley Road are unplatted fields and long deep lots. A few frame dwellings stand on Mount Hebron Road, Valley Road and Upper Mountain Avenue, with a cluster of five dwellings and a carriage house on the north side of Mount Hebron Road east of the railroad, and one small building by the track. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are shown on Mount Hebron Road, Valley Road and Laurel Pl. A compass stands at the upper left. The sheet is bordered by 67 at the top, 61 at the bottom, 68 and 65 on the right and sheet 0 on the left.
notes: Smith Avenue is probably today's College Avenue, by its position on sheet 67.
Alexander Avenue is drawn here only as a pipe line across Valley Road; its junction was not detected.
Placed from two railroad crossings and three street junctions: medium confidence.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 covers the centre of Upper Montclair around the Erie Railroad (Greenwood Lake Division) station, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the right. North Mountain Avenue forms the top edge and Park the foot of the sheet. Valley Road comes up diagonally from the lower left, passes the Upper Montclair R.R. Depot and Freight Depot and runs beside the double-tracked railroad, which crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right. Belleview Avenue and Lorraine Avenue run across the sheet, with Cooper Avenue, Summit Avenue and Wildwood Avenue as parallel cross streets and Northview Avenue and Norwood Avenue as the transverse ones. The business centre is the small group of stores and offices on the north side of Valley Road at Belleview Avenue: a bakery, drug store, barber, grocery and real estate offices, Cliffside Livery Stable, A. S. Wallace, florist, Hart's Public Livery Stable and the Osborne and Marsellis Co. coal, lumber and cement yard with its sheds beside the tracks. Public buildings are Cliffside Hose Co. No. 4 with Montclair Hook and Ladder No. 2, St. James Episcopal Church and Sunday School, the Christian Union Congregational Church, St. Cassian's R.C. Church, Commonwealth Hall and the Mt. Hebron Public School with its annex. The rest is residential, with detached two and a half storey frame dwellings on lots numbered by house along every street, and Commonwealth Field open ground. A strip marked Right of Way and a park lie at the upper left. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked.
notes: Belleview Avenue is today's Bellevue Avenue.
The sheet is drawn with north towards the right (rotation about 71 degrees).
Fits to 11 points at 1.5 m RMSE; one railroad crossing at Lorraine Avenue was rejected.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 shows a residential district of Upper Montclair between Valley Road, which crosses the top diagonally, and Park at the foot, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Lorraine Avenue forms the left edge, with Oakwood Avenue, Inwood Avenue and Fernwood Avenue running parallel to it as long narrow blocks numbered 1 to 3 on the north side, and Norwood Avenue, a curving 50 foot street, crossing the sheet from the left to the right edge and splitting off Inwood Avenue to the south. Short side streets Jerome Place, Mountain Place and Valley Place enter Valley Road at the top, and Haddon Place, Clairwill Avenue and Sunset Park Way meet Park at the bottom. Almost every lot along Lorraine, Oakwood, Inwood and Fernwood Avenues carries a two and a half storey frame dwelling with its house number, mostly detached with verandas, and a few stables and greenhouses. The Upper Montclair Lawn Tennis Club's club house stands in the middle of block 2. The south-west quarter (block 5) holds a few large stone and frame houses on big grounds, and blocks 4 and 6 on the right are largely open, with only a few dwellings. Hydrants, water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and a fire alarm box at Inwood Avenue and Park are marked. The sheet adjoins 54 above, 63 on the left, 61 and 65 on the right and 59 and 66 below.
notes: Clairwill Avenue is today's Clarewill Avenue.
Sunset Park Way is not in the modern street network (OpenStreetMap has a Sunset Park).
Fits to 12 points at 1.9 m RMSE; Fernwood Avenue / Inwood Avenue was not detected.

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 lies in Upper Montclair between Valley Road along the top and Park along the foot, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Glenwood Road and Elston Road run south from Valley Road as long parallel 50 and 60 foot streets through blocks 1 to 3 and are crossed by Norwood Avenue, which curves across the sheet from the left edge, round Valley Road's southern blocks and down to meet Alexander Avenue at the right. Alexander Avenue bends along the right edge from Valley Road to Park, with Laurel Place and Valley Place entering Valley Road at the top. The northern blocks are open fields with no street improvement beyond the lot lines; the first row of dwellings is on the east side of Alexander Avenue, where a cluster of frame dwellings, a barn and outbuildings stand between Valley Road and Norwood Avenue. South of Norwood Avenue, blocks 4 to 6 are lotted and carry scattered two and a half storey dwellings along Glenwood Road, Elston Road and Park, with a few large houses on bigger grounds and stables, and Sun Set Park Way leaves Park at the left. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at Laurel Place are marked, and the street widths of 50 to 66 feet are lettered. The sheet adjoins 61 and 62 above, 64 on the left, 68 on the right and 66 below.
notes: Sun Set Park Way is not in the modern street network.
Alexander Avenue was left out of the fit: its two junctions sat 5 to 7 m from the other control and the modern street may have been realigned.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 is the only sheet of this group drawn at 200 feet to an inch. It shows the north-eastern tip of Upper Montclair against Passaic County, with the county line crossing the top and the Town of Bloomfield (Essex County, Volume Two) line running down the right side. Grove Street enters at the top left and runs diagonally to the foot of the sheet, with Alexander Avenue crossing it to the east, and Park Street along the left edge carrying the cross streets Inwood Avenue, Clarewell Avenue and Haddon Place, which rise to Grove. Mount Hebron Road (the lettering is cut by the left edge) joins Grove at the upper left. Broad, a Bloomfield street, appears at the upper right, and Belle View Avenue at the lower right. Most of the ground is unplatted farm land, labelled with the names of owners rather than blocks: the Montclair Water Co. at the top, where a brook is coloured blue, Richard Tuers, Ellen Sigler, H. Sigler, Sarah Powelson, J. R. Tinkham, Maria Smith Estate, F. L. Francisco, Mary Mulcahy, and strips for Benj. D. Warner, Ellen S. Kessler and James H. Galloway. The Upper Montclair Country Golf Club's golf links and the Montclair Land and Improvement Co. hold the foot of the sheet. Buildings are few: scattered farm dwellings and outbuildings, with a small group near Alexander Avenue. Adjoining sheets are 68 and 65 on the left, 64 and 59 below and 60 to the lower right.
notes: Printed scale is 200 Feet = 1 Inch; the fitted scale is 1.998 px per foot.
Grove is today's Grove Street, Park today's Park Street, Clarewell Avenue today's Clarewill Avenue and Belle View Avenue today's Bellevue Avenue.
Only the south-west part of the sheet has control; the north-east (Alexander Avenue east of Grove, Broad) rests on extrapolation. Medium confidence.
Grove Street / Inwood Avenue and the Mount Hebron Road junction were not detected.

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 covers Montclair Heights in the far north-west of Upper Montclair, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Mount Hebron Road runs down the left edge to Valley Road along the foot of the sheet. Upper Mountain Avenue climbs diagonally from Mount Hebron Road at the left to the right edge, crossed by Fifth Avenue, a 60 foot street that runs the full height of the sheet from the top to Valley Road, and by Smith Avenue, which runs across the lower part. The Erie Railroad (Greenwood Lake Division) crosses the sheet in a six-track yard from the lower left to the upper right, passing the Montclair Heights R.R. Station, a small frame building with two waiting rooms and a lamp room. The Verona Township line runs across the upper left, and the Passaic County line (shown as Passaic County) cuts diagonally down the right side. Buildings are few: a handful of detached dwellings with stables and coops along Upper Mountain Avenue and in the unnamed 50 foot street at the top right, the Montclair Heights School House and its outbuildings on Mount Hebron Road, a small building near the railroad crossing, and a farm group in block 4. Blocks 1 to 4 are mostly unbuilt large lots. Sheet 62 lies to the left and 68 below.
notes: By position, Smith Avenue appears to be today's College Avenue, and Fifth Avenue to correspond to Normal Avenue, which has been realigned (Normal Avenue was left out of the fit).
Control is only a line of four points down Mount Hebron Road, so the part is a helmert fit with rotation and the right-hand side extrapolated; low confidence.
Printed scale is 100 Ft. to One Inch.

sheet-68.description: Sheet 68 shows Mount Hebron Cemetery and the north-eastern edge of Upper Montclair against the Passaic County line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Mount Hebron Road crosses the sheet from the lower left to Grove at the right, and Park runs south from it to Alexander Avenue at the bottom, while Valley Road forms the left edge. Mount Hebron Cemetery fills the upper left and centre, with burial vaults, a few small buildings and plots divided by lines. A second area marked Cemetery lies between the strips of land beside Park. The Montclair Heights Reformed Church stands on Mount Hebron Road near Valley Road with a small lot, and a group of farm buildings, a large frame house and sheds lies at the upper left. Brooks coloured blue wander through the lower half, crossing Alexander Avenue and Mount Hebron Road's southern side. Dwellings along Alexander Avenue are at the bottom left and a few farm buildings stand near Grove on the right. Hydrants, 6 and 20 inch water pipes and street widths of 50 to 66 feet are marked. The Passaic County line runs along the top. Neighbouring sheets are 67 and 62 on the left, 65 below and 66 on the right.
notes: Park is today's Park Street and Grove today's Grove Street.
The lead configured this part from four points; Grove Street / Mount Hebron Road may sit 8 to 13 m from the drawn junction.
